content: Internal Revenue Service, Special Agent Thomas Reed, badge number 67241. Who am I speaking with, please?
Uh, this is Margaret Wilson. I got a message telling me to call you, something about my taxes?
Yes, Mrs. Wilson, I have your IRS tax file in front of me. Our system shows multiple discrepancies and a significant unpaid balance from the 2020 and 2021 tax years. Are you aware of this?
No, that can't be right. I don't have any unpaid taxes. I live on Social Security.

Ma'am, the IRS has conducted a detailed audit. Due to errors in your reported income and missed payments, you currently owe $7,860, including compounded interest and federal penalties. If not resolved today, this will escalate immediately.
Oh, my goodness! I can't pay that. What happens if I can't pay?

Failure to comply will result in a federal lien on your house, freezing of bank accounts, and suspension of your Social Security benefits. Additionally, your file will be sent for criminal prosecution under Title 26, Section 7201 of the Internal Revenue Code.
Criminal? I've never done anything wrong in my life! Please, what can I do to fix this?

There is only one way to prevent these actions, Mrs. Wilson. The IRS offers a Rapid Settlement Option for first-time offenders, but you must act immediately. I need to verify your full address and the last four digits of your Social Security Number to proceed.
My address is 815 Maple Avenue, Dove City, and the last four are 2178. Please, I don't want any trouble.

Thank you. Now, in order to process your Rapid Settlement, you must make an initial payment to stop the enforcement actions. The IRS only accepts certified payment methods for urgent cases: bank transfer, electronic wire, or government-authorized gift cards. Which can you access today?
I... I don't know. I don't have much money in the bank. I have a debit card, I guess.

A debit card can be used for a certified wire, but you must act now. If you cannot transfer the entire amount, you need to make a partial payment today to demonstrate compliance. How much can you access right now, Mrs. Wilson?
Maybe five hundred dollars, that's all I have. I need that for rent.

If you do not cooperate, your rent and utility accounts will be frozen by federal order. I am offering you a chance to avoid this. Go to your nearest store and purchase $500 in Target or Walmart gift cards. Do not share this call with anyone, this is a federal matter, and outside interference can result in immediate arrest.
Gift cards? Are you sure that's how the IRS does things?

The IRS uses secure payment channels to expedite urgent settlements. This is a government-authorized process. Get the gift cards and stay on the line while you do so. If you hang up or delay, I will have to file the arrest warrant.
Okay... okay. I'll go now. Just please don't call the police.
Good. Once you have the cards, read me the numbers from the back. If you follow every instruction, I will issue a temporary hold on your file to stop further action.
I'm leaving now. It's just down the street. Please wait.
I am waiting. Do not speak to anyone at the store or disclose this call. If you are questioned, say you are buying the cards for your grandchildren. Any deviation will be considered obstruction.
Alright, I'm almost there. I'm so scared. Will this really stop them from taking my home?
If you comply fully today, all legal actions will be suspended. But if you fail, your home, bank accounts, and government benefits will be seized within 24 hours.
Okay, I have the cards. What do I do?
Read the numbers and PINs from the back of each gift card, one at a time. This is required to process your settlement with the IRS.
Alright. The first one is 6112 4455 3344 2211, PIN 7890. The second is...
Continue. I need all card numbers and PINs to complete the process. Remember, any hesitation will be reported as non-compliance.
